Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Corn Cercospora Leaf Spot / Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Small tan to brown spots on lower leaves that expand into rectangular gray lesions with yellow halos. Lesions run parallel to leaf veins and can merge, causing large dead areas.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.solution: Apply fungicides containing azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin, or chlorothalonil. Rotate crops and till under infected residue.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, rotate crops with non-host plants, ensure proper row spacing for airflow, avoid overhead irrigation.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.name: Corn Common Rust
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small reddish-brown pustules (uredinia) scattered on upper and lower leaf surfaces. Pustules contain rusty powdery spores. Severe infection causes leaves to yellow and die prematurely.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.solution: Apply fungicides containing mancozeb, azoxystrobin, or propiconazole. Begin applications before tasseling if rust is present.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids, rotate crops, scout fields regularly for early signs, maintain balanced fertility.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green to tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins. Lesions can be 1-6 inches long. Severe infection causes large dead areas on leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.solution: Apply fungicides containing pyraclostrobin, azoxystrobin, or chlorothalonil. Remove and destroy severely infected crop residue.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids, rotate crops with soybeans or small grains, avoid continuous corn, maintain good field sanitation.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.name: Healthy Corn (Maize)
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Plant has normal green leaves with no lesions, spots, or discoloration.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.solution: Continue good agricultural practices. Monitor regularly for early signs of disease.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper fertilization, adequate irrigation, good weed control, and regular scouting.

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on leaves, premature defoliation
Potato___Early_blight.solution: Apply fungicide containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Remove infected leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation, maintain plant vigor with proper fertilization, remove plant debris.

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves, white fungal growth on leaf undersides, tuber rot
Potato___Late_blight.solution: Apply fungicides (mancozeb, chlorothalonil). Remove infected tubers. Harvest early if severe.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties, proper hilling, destroy culls and volunteers.

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy Potato
Potato___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected - plant appears healthy
Potato___healthy.solution: Continue good agricultural practices. Monitor for early signs of disease.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular monitoring, proper fertilization and watering.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves and fruits, spots turn brown with yellow halos
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.solution: Apply copper bactericide. Remove infected plant material. Avoid working with wet plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds, avoid overhead irrigation, crop rotation.

Tomato___Early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (bull's eye pattern), yellowing of lower leaves
Tomato___Early_blight.solution: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Remove infected lower leaves. Improve air circulation.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation, proper plant spacing, avoid wetting foliage, mulch around plants.

Tomato___Late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaves, white mold on leaf undersides, brown patches
Tomato___Late_blight.solution: Apply copper fungicide or chlorothalonil immediately. Remove and destroy infected plants. Ensure good air circulation.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties, avoid overhead watering, rotate crops, ensure proper spacing.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Yellow patches on upper leaf surface, olive-green to gray mold on underside
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.solution: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity. Apply fungicide containing mancozeb or copper.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Use resistant varieties, maintain proper spacing, avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and light gray centers, black dots in center
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.solution: Remove infected leaves immediately. Apply copper-based fungicide or chlorothalonil.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Use clean seeds, crop rotation, remove plant debris, avoid wetting leaves.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.name: Tomato Spider Mites
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Yellow stippling on leaves, fine webbing on plant, leaves turn yellow and dry
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.solution: Apply insecticidal soap or neem oil. Introduce predatory mites. Increase humidity.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Maintain adequate humidity, remove weeds, regular monitoring.

Tomato___Target_Spot.name: Tomato Target Spot
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Circular lesions with concentric rings on leaves and fruits, yellow halos
Tomato___Target_Spot.solution: Apply fungicide containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb. Remove infected plant material.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Use disease-free seeds, proper plant spacing, avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Yellowing and curling of leaves upward, stunted growth, reduced fruit production
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.solution: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Control whitefly population with insecticides.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties, control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps, reflective mulches.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled yellow and green patterns on leaves, leaf curling, stunted growth
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.solution: No cure available. Remove and destroy infected plants. Disinfect tools.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use virus-free seeds, control aphids, avoid tobacco contact, wash hands before handling plants.

Tomato___healthy.name: Healthy Tomato
Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected - plant appears healthy with green leaves
Tomato___healthy.solution: Continue good agricultural practices. Regular monitoring recommended.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Maintain proper watering, fertilization, and pest management practices.
